profile.reading: Per QTS own site, DC6 is part of the QTS Richmond 1 campus, located at 3520 Portugee Rd, Sandston, VA 23150. The Richmond 1 campus totals 207 acres, 2.3 million sq ft of current space, and 238 MW of power capacity across six DC buildings (DC1-DC6); no per-building MW figure is published.

profile.facility_type_note: Part of QTS's Richmond, Virginia mega-campus, spanning Henrico County and Sandston. This is QTS's flagship facility story: in 2010 QTS converted a former semiconductor manufacturing site into what Wikipedia describes as a 1.3 million square foot mega data center.

reading.body:
The QTS Richmond 1 campus in Sandston totals 238 MW across six buildings on 207 acres, making it the largest published-capacity data center complex in Virginia by a narrow margin; it ranks 24th among the 326 mapped facilities in the state, but only 23 facilities in Virginia publish power figures at all, so this ranking reflects a data gap rather than a competitive position. At an assumed density of 40 kW per rack, 238 MW of total power capacity would support roughly 5,950 racks; typical AI training racks draw 40 kW or more, while inference deployments may draw less, so the usable AI capacity depends on the tenant mix and workload the operator allocates to this campus. No per-building megawatt figure is published for DC6 itself, and no details are public about whether this campus qualifies for any particular workload class through environmental certifications, resilience features, or power supply characteristics.

The Richmond 1 campus is the result of QTS converting a former semiconductor manufacturing site beginning around 2010, creating the physical infrastructure for large-scale compute deployment on real estate already zoned and built for high-intensity industrial use. The operator is Blackstone-owned as of August 2021, placing this facility within a capital partner with the scale to support expansion and to absorb the grid constraints that now throttle data center growth. Virginia's published data center capacity totals 1,375 MW across all operators, so Richmond 1 alone represents roughly 17 percent of the state's declared footprint.

The campus itself appears complete as a long-standing facility, not a growth project; the operator's own marketing describes it as flagship infrastructure, but no expansion timeline or additional power allocation is published. For a reader assessing whether this campus matters to AI scaling, the binding question is whether Blackstone and QTS can secure additional grid capacity to expand beyond 238 MW, and whether the operator is allocating vacant or future rack space to GPU-intensive workloads rather than traditional colocation tenants. Neither detail appears in published specifications.
